Below are the steps to open the speciﬁed ports for both inbound and outbound traﬃc on Windows 
10 Pro, Windows 11 Pro, and Windows Server (2016, 2019, and 2022) for both TCP and UDP: 
1. Open Ports for TCP (Inbound and Outbound): 
o 
Press Win + R to open the Run dialog. 
 
o 
Type wf.msc and press Enter to open the Windows Firewall with Advanced Security.

Alpha Web Training Document 

o 
In the leŌ pane, click on “Inbound Rules”. 
 
o 
Click “New Rule…” in the right pane.

Alpha Web Training Document 

o 
Select “Port” and click Next. 
o 
Choose “TCP” and specify the port numbers: 7180, 7181, 7121, 50003, 25, 587, 389, 
636, 5432, and 80.

Alpha Web Training Document 

o 
Select “Allow the connecƟon” and click Next. 

o 
Choose the appropriate network proﬁles (Public, Private, Domain) and click Next. 
Consult local IT Admin.

Alpha Web Training Document 

o 
Provide a name for the rule (e.g., “TCP Port 7180”) and click Finish.

Alpha Web Training Document 

o 
Repeat the above steps for each port for Outbound as well as per steps shown 
below:

2. Open Port for UDP (Inbound and Outbound): 
o 
Follow the same steps as above, but select “UDP” instead of “TCP”. 
o 
Specify the port number as 161. 
o 
Name the rule (e.g., “UDP Port 161”).
